request: Add a connecting hole of 1.7 millimetre diameter and apply 0.1 millimetre grooves to increase grip and prevent slipping.

actions.relational_constraint: The hole must connect otherwise unspecified geometry or regions.
actions.unresolved_reference: The most functionally appropriate connecting geometry is the existing coaxial clevis-pin passage through both ears. The existing bores are 1.5 millimetres in diameter, so the 1.7 millimetre connecting hole is interpreted as a coaxial enlargement of both bore segments into one continuous transverse pin passage rather than as an unrelated additional hole.
steps: Select the raised clevis interface R03 because its primary function is to connect a mating member by a transverse pin. Use the existing paired pin bores F011 and F012 as the definitive location and direction of the requested connecting hole.
Establish the hole axis from the existing coaxial cylindrical bore walls FACE 44 and FACE 46. The axis is parallel to CAD X and passes through approximately CAD y=3.510000 and z=2.943179.

Create a sketch on an outer clevis-ear side plane normal to CAD X, using FACE 78 or FACE 79 as the sketch-support reference. Project the existing bore boundary or constrain the sketch center concentric with FACE 44 and FACE 46.
Draw a circle of 1.7 millimetres diameter, corresponding to a radius of 0.85 millimetres. Fully constrain it to the common center of the existing radius-0.75-millimetre bores.

Perform a through-all subtractive extrusion parallel to CAD X, extending through the first ear F009, across the central clevis gap, and through the second ear F010. Use a symmetric or sufficiently overextended cut so that it enters through one outer side face and exits through the opposite outer side face.

This cut removes the existing bore walls FACE 44 and FACE 46 and replaces them with new coaxial radius-0.85-millimetre cylindrical walls while preserving the central gap and the two-ear clevis structure.
Do not alter the rounded ear crowns FACE 74 and FACE 68 or the ear-root support geometry. Verify that adequate material remains between the enlarged hole and each radius-1.4-millimetre ear crown.

Regenerate the solid and confirm that the resulting passage is continuous and coaxial from the first outer ear face FACE 78 to the second outer ear face FACE 79, with no residual 1.5-millimetre bore steps.

parameters.groove_dimension: 0.1 millimetres; dimension type is not specified

actions.relational_constraint: The grooves must be applied to an existing but unspecified model surface or region.
actions.unresolved_reference: The primary base mounting face FACE 77 is the surface that reacts external mounting contact and is therefore the most appropriate grip surface. For modeling, 0.1 millimetres is interpreted as groove depth. Groove width, pitch, end clearance, and pattern direction are not specified and must remain configurable or be assigned according to the applicable manufacturing standard.
steps: Select the four-point mounting base R01 and its mounting base plate F005. Localize the texture to the primary base mounting face FACE 77 at CAD y=-0.010000 because this face provides the broad seating interface and reacts contact against the supporting structure.

Create a sketch directly on FACE 77, or on a datum plane coincident with it and normal to CAD Y. Project the external boundary of FACE 77 and the four mounting-bore openings so the groove pattern can be clipped to valid mounting material.

Define a configurable shallow groove profile with a depth of 0.1 millimetres measured inward from FACE 77 toward the solid, nominally in the +CAD-Y direction. Use either narrow rectangular channels or V-shaped channels according to the intended manufacturing process.

Lay out a repeated set of linear grooves across the usable planar mounting area. To resist slipping in more than one in-plane direction, add a second intersecting set to form a cross-hatched grip pattern.

Keep the groove pattern inside the perimeter of FACE 77 and provide clearances around the four existing mounting bores associated with F001, F002, F003, and F004. Do not cut into the cylindrical bore walls FACE 50, FACE 49, FACE 51, or FACE 52.
Apply a blind pocket cut of 0.1 millimetres to the groove sketch. If V-grooves are required, use swept triangular cuts or an equivalent engraving operation constrained to the same maximum depth.

Pattern the seed groove features over FACE 77 using configurable width and pitch parameters. Trim or suppress partial grooves that would create fragile slivers at the outer perimeter, mounting-hole openings, or narrow local lobes.
Preserve the counterbore seats and rim blends on the opposite side of the base, including FACE 84, FACE 86, FACE 87, FACE 88 and their associated toroidal blends.

Regenerate and validate that the grooves remain shallow surface texture features, do not break through the mounting base, and leave sufficient continuous seating area for stable clamping while increasing friction at the support interface.
